title: First camera preview
summary: Initialize a camera and open a live preview using the Python API.
description: This tutorial checks that MEYELens is installed correctly and that your camera can be opened from Python.

sections.title: Goal
sections.body: Open a live camera preview and verify that the camera and MEYELens model can run from Python.

sections.title: Requirements
items: MEYELens installed in a dedicated Python environment
A visible eye region in the camera frame

sections.title: Tip
sections.body: If the wrong camera opens, try changing `camera_index=0` to `camera_index=1` or `camera_index=2`.

sections.title: Camera already in use
sections.body: If the camera does not open, close other applications that may be using it.

title: Record online pupil predictions
summary: Run live pupil prediction, save frame-by-frame CSV data, and send keyboard trigger pulses during acquisition.
description: This tutorial shows how to record online MEYELens pupil predictions while saving synchronized frame-level data and keyboard trigger pulses to a CSV file.
imageCaption: Online recording workflow with live prediction, preview, CSV export, and keyboard triggers.

sections.title: Goal
sections.body: Use `MeyeAsyncRecorder` to run online pupil prediction, preview the predicted pupil overlay, and save frame-by-frame results to CSV.

sections.title: What this tutorial records
items: Live camera frames processed by the MEYELens online recorder
Keyboard trigger pulses from keys `1` to `9`
A timestamped recording folder containing the final `expinfo.csv` file

sections.title: Keyboard controls
items: `s`: start recording in a new timestamped folder
`e`: stop recording and save the CSV as `expinfo.csv`
`1` to `9`: send a one-frame trigger pulse to the corresponding trigger channel

sections.title: Camera index
sections.body: The script uses `cam_ind=0` by default. If the wrong camera opens, change it to `cam_ind=1`, `cam_ind=2`, or another available camera index.

sections.title: Online prediction performance
sections.body: Online prediction speed depends on camera resolution, model size, CPU/GPU availability, and preview rendering. For time-sensitive experiments, test the real acquisition rate before collecting data.

sections.title: Automatic stop
sections.body: Set `MAX_DURATION_SEC` to a number, for example `60`, if you want the recording to stop automatically after a fixed duration.

sections.title: Output
sections.body: Each recording creates a timestamped folder inside `recordings/`. When the recording is stopped, the temporary CSV file is renamed to `expinfo.csv` for consistency across sessions.

sections.title: Trigger timing
sections.body: Trigger pulses are saved as one-frame events. Pressed keys are written on the next saved frame and then reset to zero.

sections.title: Expected result
sections.body: A live OpenCV preview window should open. During preview mode, frames are processed but not saved. After pressing `s`, online predictions and trigger values are written to CSV until you press `e` or `q`.

title: Record video with triggers
summary: Save the raw camera stream to video while recording synchronized keyboard trigger pulses to CSV.
description: This tutorial shows how to record a camera stream for later offline analysis. It saves the raw video and a synchronized trigger file without running online pupil prediction during acquisition.
imageAlt: Offline video and trigger recording tutorial
imageCaption: Offline recording workflow with raw video acquisition and frame-level trigger logging.

sections.title: What this tutorial records
items: Raw camera frames saved to a video file
Keyboard trigger pulses from keys `1` to `9`
A compact trigger `signal` column, where `0` means no trigger and `1`-`9` indicate the active trigger channel

sections.title: Keyboard controls
items: `s`: start recording in a new timestamped folder
`e`: stop recording and finalize the files
`1` to `9`: send a one-frame trigger pulse to the corresponding trigger channel

sections.title: Camera index
sections.body: The script uses `camera_index=0` by default. If the wrong camera opens, change it to `camera_index=1`, `camera_index=2`, or another available camera index.

sections.title: Frame timing
sections.body: The script uses `FrameRateManager` to control sampling at `TARGET_FPS`, but the effective frame rate still depends on camera performance, USB bandwidth, disk writing speed, and system load.

sections.title: Automatic stop
sections.body: Set `MAX_DURATION_SEC` to a number, for example `60`, if you want recording to stop automatically after a fixed duration.

sections.title: Output
sections.body: Each recording creates a timestamped folder inside `recordings/`. The trigger file is finalized as `expinfo.csv`, and the video file contains the raw camera frames.

sections.title: Trigger timing
sections.body: Trigger pulses are saved as one-frame events. Pressed keys are written on the next recorded frame and then reset to zero.

sections.title: Expected result
sections.body: A live OpenCV preview window should open. Before recording, frames are shown but not saved. After pressing `s`, raw video frames and trigger rows are saved until you press `e` or `q`.
